definitions.explanation: A disposable napkin made of paper, commonly provided at restaurants, cafes, and fast-food establishments.

examples.japanese: {紙|かみ}ナプキン⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}って→取る：00565_toru⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please pass me a paper napkin.

examples.japanese: ⟦テーブル→テーブル：04488_teeburu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{上|うえ}→上：00682_ue⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{紙|かみ}ナプキン⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{置|お}いてある→置く：01092_oku⟧。
examples.english: There are paper napkins on the table.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}ども⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{飲|の}み{物|もの}→飲み物：02929_nomimono⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦こぼした→こぼす：02104_kobosu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、{紙|かみ}ナプキン⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{拭|ふ}いた→拭く：04261_fuku⟧。
examples.english: The child spilled their drink, so I wiped it up with a paper napkin.

notes:
A compound of ⟦{紙|かみ}→紙：00712_kami⟧ (paper) and ⟦ナプキン→ナプキン：10257_napukin⟧ (napkin, from English). In Japan, restaurants often provide ⟦おしぼり→おしぼり：09726_oshibori⟧ (wet towels) instead of paper napkins, so {紙|かみ}ナプキン is more associated with Western-style restaurants and fast-food chains.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {紙|かみ}ナプキン⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{拭|ふ}く→拭く：04261_fuku⟧: to wipe with a paper napkin
- {紙|かみ}ナプキン⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{広|ひろ}げる→広げる：01981_hirogeru⟧: to unfold a paper napkin
- {紙|かみ}ナプキンホルダー: napkin holder/dispenser

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦ナプキン→ナプキン：10257_napukin⟧: napkin — the base word; in Japanese, also commonly refers to sanitary napkins
- ⟦おしぼり→おしぼり：09726_oshibori⟧: wet towel — provided at Japanese restaurants for hand-wiping
- ⟦ティッシュ→ティッシュ：08816_tisshu⟧: tissue paper — for the nose or general-purpose wiping
